He also served as chief of the Presidency of the Council of Ministers’ Court, placing him close to the machinery of government. His private wealth is opaque: court-based reporting links companies associated with him to a substantial United States property portfolio, but public evidence does not justify treating Saudi sovereign or wider royal-family assets as his personal holdings.
